editorial:
Imagine stepping back into the late sixties to see what high school felt like in Japan. You get a look at a group of students struggling with their identities, first loves, and the pressure to fit in. The vibe is very emotional and slow, focusing on the small moments that make being a teenager feel like the end of the world. You will find yourself rooting for the main kids as they try to figure out who they are while dealing with strict teachers and confused parents.

The acting feels very real, and the slow pace actually helps you feel the sadness and joy of the characters. While some parts might feel a bit too slow if you are used to modern action movies, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy stories about growing up and heartbreak, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, but if you really love old cinema, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the main couple realizes that their different social backgrounds make it impossible to stay together. Instead of a happy marriage, they decide to part ways to follow their own dreams. The movie ends with a bittersweet shot of them walking in opposite directions. It shows that growing up often means letting go of the people you love most so you can find yourself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and old school dramas.
